known_gaps.title: Acid Tracks — Phuture
known_gaps.why: source 5's opening origins sentence: 'Acid house is an electronic music genre that originated in the mid-1980s Chicago house scene. The sound's defining characteristic came from the Roland TB-303 synthesizer, and is often credited to DJ Pierre and Phuture.' Phuture invented acid house, but 'Acid Tracks' (1987) has no embedded player on the page.

known_gaps.title: Danny Rampling, Paul Oakenfold, Nicky Holloway, Mike Pickering, Graeme Park (Second Summer of Love venues/DJs)
known_gaps.why: source 5: 'Five British DJs inspired by an Ibiza holiday in summer 1987 launched the movement.' Named founders of Shoom, Future/Spectrum, Trip, and Haçienda are absent from the page despite being mentioned in prose.

known_gaps.title: The Prodigy — Firestarter or Smack My Bitch Up

known_gaps.title: Fabio & Grooverider (breakbeat hardcore founding DJs)
known_gaps.why: source 5: the article documents Fabio and Grooverider as the key DJs consolidating breakbeat hardcore on radio and in clubs. Both appear on the page but neither has a mix or signature record embedded.
